rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This config tests RNA-only modeling with a simple PCA encoder and no image data, isolating the impact of RNA representation. It clarifies whether RNA-only models are viable and provides a reference point for comparing more complex multimodal approaches.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to multiprofile and adding avgpool aggregation improves performance, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration of key design choices (profile/multimodal) while building on the RNA-only baseline, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) with RNA-only data. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) while maintaining multiprofile and avgpool aggregation could further improve performance. It isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a key design decision, without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest validation accuracy so far (0.650124). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (a more complex method) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation strategy. It builds on the promising scvi_n200 RNA encoder while exploring a key design choice with minimal other changes, balancing exploitation of the current leading configuration with exploration of a critical component.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6529). This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 encoder with transformer aggregation (same as config_006) improves performance, isolating the impact of encoder choice. It clarifies if the scvi_n200 encoder's superiority is due to architecture or if pca_n2000 could match it with transformer aggregation, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder achieve higher accuracy (65%) than singleprofile models (48-51.9%). This experiment tests whether using scvi_n200 encoder with singleprofile setting (a key design choice) can improve performance, isolating the effect of RNA encoder selection. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether scvi_n200's benefits are profile-dependent, providing critical information for prioritizing encoder choices in future experiments.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile and transformer aggregation (e.g., config_006) outperform others. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder in the same setup, isolating its effect compared to scvi_n200. It clarifies whether the new encoder improves performance, balancing exploration of key design choices with building on a promising direction.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests combining this strong RNA representation with a powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and weighted fusion, which could isolate the impact of multimodal integration. It directly extends the best-performing RNA-only configuration while exploring critical design choices (image modality, fusion method) that may yield higher accuracy.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models (e.g., config_039) outperform RNA-only models, but the RNA encoder (scvi_n200) and fusion method (weighted) are critical. This experiment tests scgpt as the RNA encoder in a similar multimodal setup (with imagenet_vit_l and transformer aggregation) to isolate the impact of the RNA encoder choice, which remains uncertain despite scvi_n200's strong performance in RNA-only settings.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while keeping RNA encoder, profile setting, aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted) identical. This isolates the effect of image encoder choice, a critical design decision, to determine if resnet50 could match or exceed vit_l performance in multimodal settings.
